thread:
evan_support: customer on private VPC hitting intermittent 502s + aborted streams to /v1/generate. Only happens when users are behind corp proxy (TLS inspection). Error in our logs: 'upstream prematurely closed connection' during token streaming. Anyone seen SNI/proxy stripping cause this?

anya_se: can you paste a repro curl + short network capture? also which proxy appliance/version?

evan_support: repro steps I'm using locally (customer provided):
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.internal:8080 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
curl shows CONNECT 200, then immediately TLS handshake fails with early close. server side session logs: "tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: unexpected message" and then 502 returned.

sre_julie: common pattern: MITM/TLS-inspection appliance terminates client TLS and opens a new TLS to our backend. If it rewrites SNI or uses a cert that doesn't include the backend hostname we can see handshake issues or ALPN mismatch for h2 streaming. Can you get a small tcpdump of the initial ClientHello from the client side?

evan_support: customer ran tcpdump and attached this excerpt (sanitized):
```
17:04:21.123456 IP client > corp-proxy: TCP 512 bytes
17:04:21.123457  "ClientHello" (no SNI extension found)
17:04:21.123459 proxy > api.redwood: CONNECT established
17:04:21.123470 proxy > api.redwood: ClientHello (SNI: internal-inspect.local)
```
They claim proxy rewrites SNI to internal-inspect.local.

mike_oncall: that explains upstream closing: when our server sees SNI internal-inspect.local it picks a cert/route that doesn't match api.redwood.example.com -> handshake mismatch. Also streaming needs ALPN h2, if proxy re-negotiates with different ALPN we can fall back incorrectly.

anya_se: steps to triage for customer: 1) run `openssl s_client -connect corp-proxy:8080 -proxy corp-proxy:8080 -servername api.redwood.example.com -tlsextdebug` from inside VPC to see what SNI actually reaches us. 2) tcpdump capture on egress to show ClientHello before/after proxy. 3) check proxy policy: is it doing TLS-termination + re-encryption? if yes, is there an option to preserve original SNI or set passthrough for our domain?

sre_julie: quick hints to share with customer:
- Repro command for them: `curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate --http2`
- Dump raw ClientHello: `sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host api.redwood.example.com'` then inspect in wireshark or `tshark -r /tmp/cap.pcap -V | grep -m1 "Extension: server_name" -A2`
- Check proxy logs for any SNI rewrite rules or virtual-host mapping.

evan_support: customer confirmed proxy product: "CorpInspect v4", default inspect mode rewrites SNI to internal-inspect.local for scanned domains. They have an allowlist feature but need guidance on what to allow.

mike_oncall: recommendation to customer (short-term): add `api.redwood.example.com` to TLS-inspection bypass (passthrough) or set Connect policy to "raw-tls passthrough" for that FQDN pattern. Long-term: if they need inspection, configure the appliance to preserve original SNI when re-encrypting and support ALPN passthrough for h2.

anya_se: temporary workaround we suggested: route Redwood traffic through a dedicated egress IP that is not inspected by CorpInspect (they already have NAT pools). This keeps traffic visible for auditing but avoids SNI rewrite. Also documented in our enterprise docs under "Private/VPC egress considerations".

infra_bot: deploy-note: logged incident RED-1246 (auto) for customer-facing status page note and docs update.

evan_support: customer applied bypass for `api.redwood.example.com` and reported immediate improvement, streams stop aborting and no more 502s. They will schedule a config change to keep limited bypass for Redwood endpoints.

mike_oncall: follow-up actions: 1) add a short KB we can paste into enterprise onboarding about "Corp proxies and TLS inspection" with commands above, 2) add a troubleshooting checklist in Console docs for VPC customers (tcpdump, openssl, check SNI/ALPN), 3) offer Dedicated egress/static IP as product option to avoid per-client proxy issues.

anya_se: copying the exact suggested text I pasted to customer for future reuse: "If you have TLS inspection enabled on your corporate proxy, please configure an allowlist rule to bypass inspection (passthrough CONNECT) for api.redwood.example.com, or ensure your appliance preserves the original SNI and ALPN when re-encrypting. If neither is possible, consider using a dedicated egress NAT pool for Redwood traffic." :thumbsup:

sre_julie: marking this resolved on our side once customer confirms after 24h. Good catch — proxy SNI rewrite + re-encryption is an easy-to-miss root cause for streaming failures.

mike_oncall: noted for runbook. Closing thread after final confirmation. :white_check_mark:
